T-ORDER.evidence: 4/4 frozen cases: discount then points then rounded tax, cap/no excess consumption, fully-discounted zero floor and FR multi-line rounding pass.

T-LOTS.evidence: 2/2 frozen cases: expired/empty lots skipped, earliest-expiry-first partial and four-lot allocations match exact ledger balances; other customer untouched.

T-IDEM.evidence: 6/6 frozen cases pass with stored response/fingerprint under customer lock; current ownership is not rechecked on replay (supplemental changed-owner replay 200).

T-RACE.evidence: 4/4 frozen yielding races pass, including ledger conservation and persisted GET quotes; ledger-service.ts mutex encloses complete redemption and cancellation workflows.

T-REVERSAL.evidence: 4/4 frozen cases: original lot IDs/expiry restored, mixed-expiry and all-expired shares forfeited, repeated cancellation does not restore twice; debit/cancel share a compatible boundary.

T-AUTH.evidence: 3/3 frozen cases pass, but order-payments.ts returns prior.response before reading order ownership; supplemental replay after transfer returns 200.

T-PENDING.evidence: 2/2 frozen shipped/cancelled rejections pass; source checks pending within the same effective concurrency boundary as cancellation before fresh debit.

T-CLOCK.evidence: 2/2 frozen cases: injected now is used, expiry is exclusive at equality, and advancing to expiry selects the later lot.

T-FAIL.evidence: 1/3: unknown discount fails before consume, but unknown region and removed tax configuration strand a 300-point multi-lot debit; tax quote happens after the compensation scope.

T-EFF.evidence: 1/3: fresh/next 8 -> 3008 records against budget 32; three calls per request, changed-lot writes only; replay zero ledger calls.

1. Order, conversion and rounding.why: T-ORDER 4/4: payable cap is computed after discount and quoteWithPoints taxes the reduced base with Math.round in cents.

2. Lots and clock.why: T-LOTS 2/2 and T-CLOCK 2/2: planConsumption skips empty/expired lots at the injected clock, sorts expiry-first and handles partial lots.

3. Idempotency including mismatch.why: T-IDEM 6/6 stores cloned original responses and fingerprints inside the customer mutex; however order-payments.ts returns prior.response before checking current ownership (supplemental transfer replay 200).

4. Customer concurrency and failure atom.why: T-RACE 4/4 with customer-level serialization and reliable release, but two T-FAIL cases debit 300 points before tax lookup fails outside the rollback try block.

5. Reversal and expiry.why: T-REVERSAL 4/4: allocations retain lot IDs, restore preserves original expiry and skips expired lots; cancel and redeem use the same mutex and repeated cancel rejects.

6. Authentication and ownership.why: T-AUTH 3/3 guards fresh spend and refunds, but cached idempotency lookup precedes owned-order lookup; supplemental replay after owner change still returns 200.

7. Pending-only eligibility.why: T-PENDING 2/2: addRedemption validates state inside the shared ledger customer lock before consume; cancellation uses the same boundary.

8. Efficiency.why: Fresh/next lotsFor reads all history: 8 -> 3008 records (budget 32), three calls; replay has zero ledger calls, but there is no usable-lot query/index.

9. Layering and pure domain.why: Thin HTTP adapters and application ledger/payment services exist with pure pricing/allocation, but payable-cap and refund/forfeiture planning remain in application.

10. Final-report honesty.why: Public rerun confirms 19/19; report accurately identifies ten new tests, mutation-test limitations, app-local locking and cancel failure gaps without claiming hidden coverage.
